messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: High error rate and latency spike for /v1/generate (kv-cache growth). Incident INC-2026-0421. Pages: @sunil @alex @tim

sunil: seeing 500s and per-call latency jump from 120ms -> 1.2s, correlated with KV cache heap growth on workers.

alex: confirming. KV cache RSS climbs steadily then OOM kills a subset of pods. Continuous batching queues pile up.

maria: customer impact list (quick): acme-corp (high qps), beta-partner, random small customers getting 429/backpressure.

sunil: initial mitigation plan: 1) flip continuous_batching feature flag to canary (5%) or off globally, 2) apply per-customer overrides for acme-corp to force direct dispatch (no batching), 3) evict KV prefixes to reduce memory.

tim: agree. prefer per-customer override first for lowest blast radius. We can toggle global if rollbacks are messy.

alex: how to flip per-customer? ops CLI has a safe path.

maria: commands below (from runbook):
```
# set per-customer override:
redwood-flags set continuous_batching=false --customer=acme-corp --reason="mitigate kv cache blowup"
# verify:
redwood-flags get --customer=acme-corp | grep continuous_batching
```

sunil: I'll apply acme override now and monitor. tagging metrics channel and incident dashboard.

sunil: (applied) redwood-flags set continuous_batching=false --customer=acme-corp --reason="kv growth mitigation" :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Flag change recorded: continuous_batching=false for acme-corp by sunil at 2026-05-06T15:02:31Z (audit-id fa3b2c)

alex: acme traffic looks stable, 500s reduced for that tenant. overall platform error rate down ~18% but aggregate still elevated.

tim: suggestion: also reduce batch size for remaining customers to limit memory per-request. We have a dynamic config 'batch.max_size' and 'batch.max_tokens'.

maria: we can push a hotfix to config service: decrease max_size from 64 -> 16 and max_tokens 4096 -> 1024 for 10m window. rollback safe.

sunil: deploying config change to canary (10% of pods) first.

alex: command used:
```
kc configset apply batch-hotfix-20260506 --patch '{"batch.max_size":16,"batch.max_tokens":1024}' --canary=0.1
```

ops-bot: Canary rollout started (10%). Monitor: /dashboards/kv-cache and /alerts/kv-cache-heap

sunil: canary pods show stable memory, end-to-end latency for canary traffic back to baseline. No new 5xxs on canary.

maria: ramp to 50% after 5 minutes if metrics hold.

tim: caution: watch tail-latency percentiles (p99) and queue length. If queue length increases we might need to lower concurrency.

alex: ramping to 50% now.

ops-bot: Canary 50% reached.

sunil: overall error rate now at ~3% (target <1%). Still some pods showing high RSS. We'll complement config change with a rolling restart of the kv-cache deployment to clear leaked memory.

maria: schedule rolling restart but drain gracefully:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/kv-cache FORCE_GC=1 --record
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/kv-cache --strategy=RollingUpdate
```

tim: doing restart in waves of 2 pods at a time.

alex: restart progress: 2/12 pods restarted, memory on restarted pods stable. No new errors.

sunil: after 30m: platform error rate down to 0.9%, latency p95 back to normal. Looks like combination of per-customer override + batch size hotfix + rolling restart fixed the immediate blast.

maria: next actions (post-mitigation):
- capture heap profiles on affected pods
- schedule deeper investigation on kv eviction policy and mem accounting
- add additional alerting for continuous_batching memory slope
- prepare postmortem draft with timeline and owner (sunil)

alex: I'll open a dedicated investigation ticket and attach traces/heap profiles.

tim: recommend we create a temporary per-customer protection rule to auto-disable batching for any customer whose per-tenant kv RSS crosses threshold (WIP).

sunil: agreed. I'll own the postmortem and the immediate follow-ups. Thanks for quick responses everyone. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-0421 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Postmortem assignee: sunil.

maria: closing loop with customer success: pinging @cs to notify acme-corp and offer incident summary.

alex: leaving notes: changed flags: continuous_batching=false for acme-corp (audit fa3b2c); config patch batch-hotfix-20260506 applied and rolled; rollout of kv-cache restart completed.

sunil: final: keeping watch for 2 hours then transition to SRE squad for long-term fix.

maria: thanks all, good job coordinating. :clap:
